en.headline: Retired woman loses HK$2.9 million in romance scam
en.dek: Police said at least 18 online romance frauds were reported in a week, with combined losses near HK$7.8 million, after a 71-year-old was lured into a fake investment.
body: A 71-year-old retired woman lost nearly HK$2.9 million after a man she met on Facebook posed as a power company employee, formed an online relationship and steered her into a bogus investment, police said.

According to the force's CyberDefender page, the man introduced what he called a sure-win waste-recycling project in Singapore and had the woman download a fake investment app. An online 'customer service' agent then told her to open an account and deposit money. When she tried to withdraw the rising balance shown on the platform, the agent refused. The man later claimed he had been arrested in Singapore for money laundering and asked her for bail and legal fees, and to pay cash into a designated e-wallet at a cryptocurrency shop.

Police said the woman drained her savings and borrowed from friends and finance companies, making 17 transfers totalling nearly HK$2.9 million. She learned she had been deceived after a lender chased the debt and she asked her daughter for help. Officers said at least 18 online romance scams were reported in the past week, with losses close to HK$7.8 million, and urged the public to treat online courtship that turns to investment requests as a warning sign.

zh.headline: 七旬婦墮網上情緣騙局失近290萬
zh.dek: 警方公布過去一周至少18宗網上情緣騙案、合共接近780萬元，其中一名71歲退休女子被誘投資後轉賬17次。
body: 警方表示，一名71歲退休女子在Facebook結識自稱電力公司職員的男子，發展成素未謀面的網戀後，被誘投資一項聲稱穩賺的新加坡廢料回收項目，先後損失近290萬元。
警方「守網者」專頁指，男子取得事主信任後，誘使她下載假冒投資平台應用程式，再由所謂線上客服指示開戶及存入資金。平台顯示結餘不斷上升，但事主要求提款時遭各種藉口拒絕。男子其後誑稱自己在新加坡因洗黑錢被捕，要求她支付保釋金和律師費，並親自到加密貨幣找換店把現金存入指定電子錢包。
事主花光積蓄，更向朋友及財務公司借貸，分17次轉出近290萬元。直至財務公司追債，她向女兒借錢周轉，才揭發受騙。警方稱過去一周接獲至少18宗網上情緣騙案，總損失接近780萬元，呼籲市民若網戀對象轉而要求投資或轉賬，應立即提高警覺。
